ops.title: cc-interact v0.32.1 released — the Stop fix is consumable, and go1.26.5 now has five called stdlib advisories
ops.body:
Two facts from cutting the v0.21 flag-day release chain on 2026-08-16. Recorded in daemonkit because it is the substrate all of this hangs off; the commits cited live in cc-interact.

## 1. cc-interact v0.32.1 is tagged at `fa301187c525074795a3139e091c792af470a381`

It carries `2614d0a`, the fix for `Launcher.Stop` reusing the Program-bearing `Daemon` that `EnsureCurrent` needs — which made daemonkit's absence proof resolve `~/.daemonkit/bin/<label>`, a copy only `Ensure` ever places. On a machine that never ensured this era the resolve failed, `Stop` returned before the removal, and the surviving plist relaunched the daemon. Every consumer pinned `v0.32.0` (= `d2304fd`), which predates it, so none of cc-present, cc-review, or cc-orchestrate could remove its own LaunchAgent.

**cc-interact publishes no GitHub Release by design** — `release.yml` only builds and publishes the `@cc-interact/react` npm package. Go consumers resolve the pushed tag directly through the module proxy, so a pushed tag *is* the release. Do not go looking for a missing release object.

Release convention, confirmed by reading how `v0.32.0` was cut: the commit itself writes the dated `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD` heading, an empty `## [Unreleased]` stays above it, a compare link is appended to the reference block, and the tag (lightweight, matching `v0.32.0`) points at that commit.

Proxy note: after pushing the tag, `https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/yasyf/cc-interact/@latest` reported v0.32.1 immediately while `@v/v0.32.1.info` kept 404ing with `unknown revision` for 10+ minutes — a stale negative-cache entry from probes made before the push, not a bad tag. Retry rather than re-cutting anything.

## 2. go1.26.5 has five called stdlib advisories; the whole fleet is exposed

The CI `vuln` job went red on the first push since 2026-08-08 with no Go source changing. GO-2026-6089, GO-2026-5972, GO-2026-5026 and two more land in code these modules actually call: `http.Server.Serve`, `http.Client.Do`, and `asn1.Unmarshal` reached through `daemonkit.Client.Control`. All five are fixed in go1.26.6.

The fix applied in `fa30118` and proven green in CI: add a `toolchain go1.26.6` line to `go.mod`. **Bump `toolchain`, not the `go` directive** — the `go` directive stays at 1.26.5, so consumers are not forced up by repinning (a `toolchain` line in a dependency's go.mod does not propagate).

Every fleet module currently declares `go 1.26.5` with no toolchain line except daemonkit, which already uses the low-`go`/explicit-`toolchain` shape (`go 1.26.3` + `toolchain go1.26.5`). cc-present, cc-review, cc-orchestrate, and cc-skills/plugins/codex will each go red on their next push until they take the same bump. **daemonkit is frozen at v0.21.4 and does not get this bump** — its `toolchain go1.26.5` line will fail a vuln job the moment anything is pushed there, which is a known consequence of the freeze rather than a new defect.

Bracket for the fix, not a green-only reading: red at `0c1fc2c7` under go1.26.5 (CI run 31935762282, `Found in: net/http@go1.26.5`, 5 vulns), green at `fa30118` under go1.26.6 (CI run 31935983112), the toolchain line the only difference.
